mainTopic: Dividing an estate between adult and minor heirs, and whether a husband counts as a buyer or an heir of his wife's property
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about produce still attached to the ground (מחוברין). עולא explains that a father wants his son to get it together with the land, but an outside buyer must pay for it. A new משנה then teaches that adult and minor heirs, whether sons or daughters, do not support themselves from each other's share; they divide equally. Wedding costs paid by the father during his lifetime stay with whoever received them. Daughters are fed from an estate that sons inherit, but not from one that other daughters inherit. In the גמרא, רבא rules that the eldest brother may keep clothing he took from the shared estate, and the משנה's ban is limited to an idle brother (שרכא). רב יהודה explains that minors may match only weddings paid from the estate after the father's death. Finally, אבוה בר גניבא asks whether a husband is a לוקח or a יורש of his wife's property. Several proofs are brought and pushed back, and אביי begins quoting a משנה about יובל that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא says attached produce is appraised for the buyer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that attached produce goes with the land, using a ברייתא that says the buyer must pay for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: the court appraises the produce still attached to the ground for the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking what came just before. The earlier ruling suggested that produce still attached to the ground goes with the land to the son, but this ברייתא suggests otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling before this implied that attached produce (מחוברין) belongs to whoever gets the land. The ברייתא says the court sets a price on the attached produce and the buyer must pay for it. That treats attached produce as separate property that still belongs to the heirs, which looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught (a ברייתא is quoted as a challenge)
The court appraises / sets a price
Produce still attached to the ground

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
The court appraises the attached produce for the buyer!
phrases.notes: The buyer has to pay the heirs for the produce, so it seems the attached produce did not come free with the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier inference from the previous משנה that attached produce goes with the land.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that attached produce belongs to the son who receives the land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats attached produce as a separate item the buyer must pay for, so it does not automatically go with the land.

steps.title: עולא: a son gets it, another person does not
steps.stepSummary: עולא resolves the contradiction: the son gets attached produce with the land, but a different buyer must pay for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is not difficult. Here it is talking about his son, and there it is talking about another person. This is because a person's mind is close to his son.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge by showing the two sources are talking about different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ruling is about a father giving land to his own son. We assume the father wanted the son to have everything, including the attached produce. The ברייתא is about another person, who has no such closeness, so he gets only the land and must pay for the produce.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
Here... there (each source is about a different case)

keyTerms.term: דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם קְרוֹבָה אֵצֶל בְּנוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A person's mind favors his son

steps.whatToRemember: A person is assumed to want to give generously to his son, so the son gets the attached produce with the land. Another person, like an outside buyer, does not get that assumption.

phrases.english: עולא said: It is not difficult;
here it is about his son, there it is about another person;
phrases.notes: "Here" is our ruling about the son; "there" is the ברייתא about the buyer.

phrases.english: since a person's mind
is close to his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (son versus another person)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and our ruling seemed to contradict each other about attached produce.
steps.terutzMaskana: Attached produce goes to the son because of the father's closeness to him; another buyer must pay for it.

steps.title: Adult and minor sons split the estate equally
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: when a father leaves adult and minor sons, neither group lives off the other's money; they divide equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man left adult sons and minor sons, the adults are not supported from the minors' money, and the minors are not fed from the adults' money. Instead, they divide equally.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how an estate is divided when some of the sons are adults and some are minors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adults may need money for their own living, and minors need to be fed. The משנה rules that no one uses the shared estate in a way that eats into the other group's portion. Each son gets an equal share and pays his own expenses from it.

phrases.english: משנה: If he left adult sons and minor sons –

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַגְּדוֹלִים מִתְפַּרְנְסִין עַל יְדֵי הַקְּטַנִּים,
phrases.english: the adults are not supported at the expense of the minors,
and the minors are not fed at the expense of the adults,
rather, they divide equally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adult and minor heirs split the estate equally, and each supports himself from his own share.

steps.title: Weddings: what the father gave stays given
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: if the adults married, the minors marry too, but the minors cannot demand the same wedding money the father gave the adults during his life.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the adults married, the minors marry. But if the minors say, 'We will marry the same way you married,' the court does not listen to them. Whatever their father gave them, he gave.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the cost of weddings. It sets a limit on what the younger sons can demand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gifts the father gave the older sons for their weddings while he was alive belong to them. They are not taken out of the shared estate to pay the minors back. The minors cannot claim extra wedding money from the estate to match what their older brothers already got.

keyTerms.meaning: We (the court) do not listen to them
What he gave, he gave (the gift stands)

steps.confusionAlert: The first line ("the minors marry") and the later lines ("we do not listen to them") can look like they clash. The גמרא will explain how they fit together.
steps.whatToRemember: Heirs share the estate equally. Gifts the father gave in his lifetime stay with whoever got them and are not balanced out among the brothers.

phrases.english: If the adults married, the minors marry.
And if the minors said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אָנוּ נוֹשְׂאִין כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנְּשָׂאתֶם אַתֶּם –
phrases.english: We are marrying in the same way that you married –
we do not listen to them;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַה שֶׁנָּתַן לָהֶם אֲבִיהֶם, נָתַן.
phrases.english: rather, what their father gave them, he gave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, applying equal division to wedding costs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Minors cannot demand wedding money matching the father's lifetime gifts to the adults; those gifts stay with the adults.

steps.title: Adult and minor daughters divide the estate equally
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that when a father leaves only daughters, some adult and some minor, neither group is supported from the other's funds. They split the estate equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the father left adult and minor daughters, the adults are not provided for from the minors' money, and the minors are not fed from the adults' money. Instead, they divide equally.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now applies the same rule it gave for sons to a case where only daughters inherit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the sons in step 3, each daughter gets an equal share of the estate. Each one then pays for her own needs from her own share. No group can spend the shared money on itself before the split.

phrases.english: If he left adult and minor daughters,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַגְּדוֹלוֹת מִתְפַּרְנְסוֹת עַל יְדֵי הַקְּטַנּוֹת,
phrases.english: the adults are not provided for from the minors' funds,
and the minors are not fed from the adults' funds,
rather, they divide equally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the sons' rule from step 3, now for daughters
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adult and minor daughters who inherit do not support one another from the shared estate; they divide it equally.

steps.title: Minor daughters marry too, but cannot demand the adults' wedding standard
steps.stepSummary: If the adult daughters married, the minor daughters also marry from the estate. They cannot demand to be married at the level the adults were married in their father's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the adult daughters married, the minor daughters marry too. If the minors say, 'We will marry the same way you married,' the court does not listen to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the wedding rule from step 4 to daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the adults married using estate money, the minors also get money for their weddings. But whatever the father chose to spend on the adults while he was alive does not set the standard. The minors cannot claim the same amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The court does not listen to them

phrases.english: If the adults married, the minors marry.
And if the minors say:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אָנוּ נוֹשְׂאוֹת כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנְּשָׂאתֶם אַתֶּם –
phrases.english: We are marrying in the same way that you married,
they are not listened to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the sons' wedding rule from step 4, now for daughters
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Minor daughters may marry from the estate, but not at the level the father gave the adult daughters in his lifetime.

steps.title: Daughters are supported by sons, but not by other daughters
steps.stepSummary: The משנה points out a difference: daughters are fed from the estate when sons inherit it, but they are not fed from it when other daughters inherit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a stringency regarding daughters compared with sons: daughters are fed from the sons' estate, but they are not fed from the daughters' estate.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by showing where daughters' rights are different from sons' rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there are sons, the daughters receive food and support from the estate the sons inherit, based on the conditions of their mother's כתובה. When only daughters inherit, that right does not exist, so a younger daughter cannot claim support from her sisters. Each daughter just takes her equal share.

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency: a way in which the law is stricter

steps.confusionAlert: The daughters do have a support right, but only against sons who inherit. Against other daughters, they get only an equal share.
steps.whatToRemember: Sons and daughters who inherit together with siblings of their own kind all divide equally. Only daughters have a support claim, and only against the sons.

phrases.english: This is a stringency with daughters compared to sons:
that the daughters are fed from the sons,
but they are not fed from the daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a contrast between daughters and sons after giving the parallel rules
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daughters are supported from an estate inherited by sons, but not from one inherited by other daughters.

steps.title: The eldest brother who dressed from the shared estate keeps what he took
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבא: if the eldest brother took clothing from the shared estate, what he did stands. The other brothers cannot deduct it from his share.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: this eldest brother who dressed and covered himself from the household property, what he did is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a new ruling from רבא about one brother using shared estate money for his own clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said brothers do not live off each other's money (step 3). רבא adds a limit: clothing the eldest brother already took from the shared estate is not charged back to him. His appearance helps the whole household.

keyTerms.meaning: The household, meaning the shared estate
What he did is done; it stands

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rava says:
This eldest of the brothers
who wore clothes and covered himself from the house,
phrases.notes: "The house" means the property the brothers still own together before splitting it.

phrases.english: what he did is done.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא הַאי גְּדוֹל אֲחֵי דִּלְבַשׁ וְאִיכַּסִּי מִבֵּיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא with a ruling that narrows the משנה's rule against heirs using shared funds
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clothing the eldest brother took from the shared estate is not deducted from his share.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from the משנה: adults may not be supported from the minors' funds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: the adults are not supported from the minors' funds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's ruling that the eldest brother may keep clothing he took from the shared estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says an adult brother cannot take support from the shared estate at the minors' expense. Clothing seems like a kind of support, so רבא's ruling looks like it goes against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in the משנה)? This opens a challenge from a source.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
The adults are not supported from the minors' funds!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the eldest brother's clothing taken from the estate stays his
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids adults from taking support from the shared estate at the minors' expense, and clothing is a form of support.

steps.title: The משנה speaks of an idle brother
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's rule is about a שרכא, a brother who is idle.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is talking about a שרכא, an idle person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה and רבא are talking about different kinds of brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's ban covers a brother who does nothing for the family. רבא's case is understood as the brother who represents and runs the family's affairs, so his respectable clothing helps everyone. That is why it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: an idle person, someone who does not work for the family

phrases.english: The משנה is about an idle person.
phrases.notes: A שרכא is someone who just wanders around and doesn't work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the משנה and רבא speak of different brothers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids every adult brother from taking clothing from the estate.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is limited to an idle brother. רבא's eldest brother is different.

steps.title: Isn't the idle-brother case obvious?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is about an idle brother, why would it need to say he can't take from the estate?
steps.simpleTranslation: An idle person? That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer: if the משנה only means an idle brother, it seems to teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of course a brother who does nothing for the family can't spend shared money on himself. So the גמרא asks what the משנה adds by saying so.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new)

phrases.english: An idle person — that's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה refers to a שרכא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the משנה states something everyone already knows.

steps.title: We might have thought the brothers want him dressed well
steps.stepSummary: Without the משנה, we might think the brothers want even an idle brother dressed respectably. The משנה teaches otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: it suits them that he not look disgraceful. So it teaches us that he still may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the משנה's ruling is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could argue that a shabby-looking brother embarrasses the whole family, so they'd be happy to pay for his clothes. The משנה teaches that this is not enough, and an idle brother still may not take from the estate.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (the mistaken idea the source comes to rule out)

steps.whatToRemember: An idle brother may not take clothing from the shared estate, even though looking respectable would honor the family. רבא's rule covers a different kind of brother.

phrases.english: You might have said:
it suits them that he not look disgraceful;
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the other brothers. A shabby brother would make the family look bad.

phrases.english: so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a reasonable mistaken idea (מהו דתימא) that the משנה rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The brothers would want even an idle brother dressed respectably.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even so, an idle brother may not take from the shared estate.

steps.title: What does 'the adults married, the minors marry' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about marrying and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If the adults married, the minors marry.' What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, asking what the משנה's line about weddings means. This sets up רב יהודה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line is unclear. It could mean the minors always get to match the adults' weddings, or it could apply only in certain cases. The גמרא wants it spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? (a request to explain unclear wording)

phrases.english: 'If the adults married, the minors marry.'
What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the clothing discussion to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning and scope of the משנה's line 'if the adults married, the minors marry'

steps.title: רב יהודה: only weddings after the father's death
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the minors match only weddings paid from the estate after the father died. They cannot match weddings the father paid for while alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: this is what it means. If the adults married after their father died, the minors also marry after he died, paid from the estate. But if the adults married while their father was alive, and after his death the minors say 'We'll marry the way you married,' we don't listen to them. Whatever their father gave, he gave.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by limiting the משנה's line to weddings after the father's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the father dies, everything belongs to the shared estate. If the adults used estate money for their weddings, the minors get the same. Money the father gave while he was alive was his own personal gift, so the minors have no claim to match it from the estate.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (introducing an explanation)
we do not listen to them (their claim is rejected)

steps.whatToRemember: Minors may match their older siblings' weddings only when those weddings were paid from the estate after the father died. What the father gave while alive was his own gift.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the משנה as 'the minors always get weddings equal to the adults'. רב יהודה limits it to weddings after the father's death.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains Steps 4 and 6 of the משנה: a father's gifts during his life are separate from the estate the heirs share.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: this is what it is saying:
If the adults married after their father's death,
the minors marry after their father's death too.
But if the adults married during their father's lifetime,
and the minors said after their father's death:
'We will marry the same way you married,'
we do not listen to them;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מָה שֶׁנָּתַן לָהֶן אֲבִיהֶן – נָתַן.
phrases.english: rather, whatever their father gave them, he gave.
phrases.notes: 'Them' here means the adults. That money was the father's own gift and doesn't come out of the estate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The line applies only when the adults married after the father's death using estate funds. Weddings the father paid for in his lifetime cannot be claimed by the minors.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A father's gifts during his lifetime stay with the one who got them. Only estate spending after his death must be matched equally.

steps.title: Is the husband a buyer or an heir of his wife's property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about adult and minor daughters. אבוה בר גניבא asks רבא whether a husband counts as a לוקח or a יורש of his wife's property, when she borrowed before the wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: the father left adult and minor daughters. אבוה בר גניבא sent a question to רבא: Teach us, our rabbi. A woman borrowed money, spent it, and then got married. Is her husband like a buyer of her property, or like an heir?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion on the משנה's case of adult and minor daughters. אבוה בר גניבא asks רבא a question about the status of a husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a woman marries, her property comes under her husband's control. The question is how to define that transfer. Does the husband get it like someone who bought it (a לוקח), or like someone who inherited it (a יורש)?

keyTerms.meaning: She borrowed and spent the money
"Let our teacher instruct us", a polite way of asking a rabbi a question

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the daughters themselves. The question is about any married woman who has a debt. The גמרא will soon connect it back to the daughters in the משנה.

phrases.english: He left adult and minor daughters.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ אֲבוּהּ בַּר גְּנִיבָא לְרָבָא,
phrases.english: Avuh bar Geneiva sent to Rava:
Let our teacher instruct us:
She borrowed and spent it,
and then she went and got married —
is the husband a buyer,
or is he an heir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic tied to the משנה's case of adult and minor daughters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a husband's hold on his wife's property gives him the status of a לוקח or of a יורש.

steps.title: Why it matters: collecting an oral loan
steps.stepSummary: The question explains the practical difference. An oral loan (מלוה על פה) cannot be collected from buyers, but it can be collected from heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is he a buyer? Then an oral loan cannot be collected from buyers. Or perhaps he is an heir? Then an oral loan can be collected from heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The question continues. It spells out what difference it makes whether the husband is a buyer or an heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan without a document is not publicly known, so buyers are protected from it. Heirs, though, must pay their father's debts even without a document. So if the husband is a לוקח, the lender loses. If he is a יורש, the lender can collect from him.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan made orally, with no written document

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole סוגיא. The status of the husband decides whether the lender can get paid.

phrases.english: Is he a buyer —

phrases.aramaic: וּמִלְוֶה עַל פֶּה אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה מִן הַלָּקוֹחוֹת;
phrases.english: and an oral loan is not collected from buyers;
or perhaps he is an heir —

phrases.aramaic: וּמִלְוֶה עַל פֶּה גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין?
phrases.english: and an oral loan is collected from heirs?

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹקֵחַ הָוֵי וּמִלְוֶה עַל פֶּה אֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה מִן הַלָּקוֹחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical result of the question in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the lender of an oral loan collect from the husband, depending on whether he is a לוקח or a יורש?

steps.title: רבא's proof from the משנה about the daughters
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a proof from the משנה. The minors marry "from the husband". That suggests they collect their wedding money back from the older sisters' husbands, which would make a husband like an heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: We learned in the משנה: If the adult daughters married, the minor daughters marry. Doesn't this mean: the adults married and brought money to their husbands, so the minors marry with money taken from those husbands?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers using the משנה. He reads it to mean that the younger sisters can take their wedding money back from the older sisters' husbands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The older sisters took wedding money from the shared estate. That is like an oral debt they owe their younger sisters. If the younger sisters can collect it from the husbands, then husbands must be like heirs, because an oral loan is never collected from buyers.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned it (in a משנה)
What, is it not...? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: He said to him: We learned:
If the adults married, the minors marry.
What, is it not
that the adults married to a husband —
phrases.notes: "To a husband" means each one brought money from the estate to her husband for the wedding.

phrases.english: the minors marry from the husband?
phrases.notes: The minors take their share back from what the older sisters' husbands received.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 15–16 using the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband is like a יורש, so an oral debt can be collected from him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: נשאו גדולות ישאו קטנות, read as "the minors marry from the husband".

steps.title: The proof is rejected: the minors take from the estate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's reading. The משנה only means that the minors may also bring wedding money to their own husbands, just as the adults did. They do not collect anything from the older sisters' husbands.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means: the adults married and brought money to their husbands, so the minors also marry and bring money to their husbands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It offers another reading of the משנה that says nothing about collecting from the husbands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "from the husband" are replaced with "to the husband". The minors are just as entitled as their sisters to take wedding money from what is left in the estate. Since nobody collects from the older sisters' husbands, the משנה proves nothing about whether a husband is a לוקח or a יורש.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof is pushed off: the משנה can mean the minors take their wedding money from the remaining estate. The next step challenges this reading with רבי חייא's ברייתא.

phrases.english: No;
the adults married to a husband —
the minors marry to a husband.
phrases.notes: Each younger sister gets her own wedding money from what is left of the estate, just like her older sisters did.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא; נָשְׂאוּ גְּדוֹלוֹת לְבַעַל יִשְּׂאוּ קְטַנּוֹת לְבַעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not decide the original question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as the minors taking money "to" their own husbands from the estate, not "from" their sisters' husbands, so it does not show that a husband pays oral debts.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the minors collect from the husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection in step 18 by quoting רבי חייא, who clearly contrasts 'to the husband' with 'from the husband.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רבי חייא taught: if the older daughters married and brought money to a husband, the younger daughters marry and collect from the husband!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading from step 18, which said the minors take nothing from the older sisters' husbands. It quotes a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא sets 'to the husband' against 'from the husband.' That contrast means the minors take money back from the older sisters' husbands. So רבא's original reading in step 17 seems right after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening for a challenge

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rabbi Chiyya teach:
If the adult daughters married, bringing money to a husband,
the minor daughters marry, collecting from the husband!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 18 and supports רבא's reading from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 18's claim that the minors collect nothing from the older sisters' husbands.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא's 'to the husband' versus 'from the husband' shows that the minors collect back from the husbands.

steps.title: Wedding funding may be different because it is public
steps.stepSummary: Even if the minors collect from the husbands, this proves nothing about an oral loan. Wedding funding is publicly known, so it works like a written loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps wedding funding is different, since it is publicly known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that the minors collect from the husbands. But it says this still does not answer אבוה בר גניבא's question about an oral loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oral loan cannot be collected from buyers because buyers had no warning. Everyone knows that a father's estate is set aside for his daughters' weddings. So the younger sisters could collect from the husbands even if a husband counts as a buyer.

phrases.english: Perhaps wedding funding is different,
since it has publicity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grants the reading in step 19 but blocks it from answering the original question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the משנה or ברייתא as proof about oral loans. It does not reject the reading 'from the husband.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Wedding funding is public, like a written loan, so it does not show how a husband is treated for a private oral loan.

steps.title: רב פפא brings רבין's letter about a widow's support
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא quotes a ruling: a widow keeps getting food from her late husband's property even after their daughter marries and then dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: Isn't this what רבין sent in his letter? If a man died and left a widow and a daughter, the widow is fed from his property. If the daughter married, the widow is still fed from his property. If the daughter died, רב יהודה, son of the sister of רבי יוסי בן חנינא, said: the case came before me, and they ruled that the widow is still fed from his property.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a new proof for the question of buyer versus heir. Here he lays out the case. In the next step he explains why it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the daughter dies, her husband inherits from her, so the property is now fully his. Even so, the widow's right to food stays attached to it. That is the fact רב פפא will build on.

keyTerms.meaning: She is fed, receiving food support

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava,
Isn't this what Ravin sent in his letter:
One who died and left a widow and a daughter,
his widow is fed from his property.
If the daughter married,
his widow is still fed from his property.
If the daughter died,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בֶּן אֲחוֹתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי [בֶּן חֲנִינָא]:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of the sister of Rabbi Yosei ben Chanina, said:
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

phrases.english: This case happened with me,
and they said: his widow is fed from his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from wedding funding was turned aside, a new proof is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband counts as a יורש of his wife's property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבין's letter: the widow is fed from the property even after it passes to the daughter's husband.

steps.title: Why the widow's support shows the husband is an heir
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains his proof: the widow keeps her support only if the daughter's husband is an heir. A buyer would not owe her food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say the husband is an heir; that is why the widow is fed from the property. But if you say he is a buyer, why is she fed from the property?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his proof by showing why the case only works if a husband counts as an heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heirs must keep feeding the widow from the estate, but people who bought the property do not have to. Since the widow still gets her support from the daughter's husband, he must be treated like an heir.
steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's proof: the widow is still fed from property held by the daughter's husband. Buyers do not owe a widow food, so the husband is treated like a יורש.

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say he is an heir,
that is why the widow is fed from his property;
but if you say he is a buyer,
why is she fed from his property?
phrases.notes: Buyers of inherited property don't have to feed the widow, so a buyer would owe her nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind the case brought in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That a husband counts as a יורש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The widow keeps her support from property held by the daughter's husband. This works only if he is an heir, since a buyer would not owe it.

steps.title: אביי asks why Ravin's letter was needed
steps.stepSummary: אביי questions the need for רבין's letter. He suggests we would have known its ruling anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If רבין had not sent his letter, would we not have known this?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a sharp question: was רבין's letter really telling us anything new? This line sets up the next step, where he shows where we could have learned the ruling ourselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא just used רבין's letter to show that the husband counts as a יורש. אביי asks whether the letter was needed at all. He claims an earlier משנה already settles the husband's status, and the next step begins quoting it.

keyTerms.meaning: If not, if it were not for
He sent (a letter or ruling, usually from ארץ ישראל)
An אמורא who often carried rulings from ארץ ישראל to בבל

steps.confusionAlert: אביי's line is about whether רבין's letter was needed. The משנה he brings as his source starts in the next step and continues past this amud.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
If Ravin had not sent [his letter],
would we not have known?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דִּשְׁלַח רָבִין, אֲנַן לָא יָדְעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב פפא's proof in steps 21–22 by asking whether רבין's letter was needed, since an earlier משנה already speaks to the husband's status.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבין's letter, which רב פפא used to settle the husband's status.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an existing משנה already settles the husband's status, רבין's letter was not needed to show it.

steps.title: אביי begins quoting the משנה about יובל
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts quoting a משנה that lists properties that do not return in the יובל year. The list begins with the בכור's portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: These do not go back in the יובל year: the בכור's portion...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings his source. He starts reading a משנה that lists properties that stay with their new holder in the יובל year instead of going back to the original owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the יובל year, sold fields go back to their original owners. This משנה lists exceptions, starting with the בכור's double portion, which stays with him. The item that matters for אביי's point about the husband comes next in the list, past this line.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? It introduces an earlier source.
Go back, return (to the original owner)
The 50th year, when sold fields return to their owners
The firstborn's extra share of the inheritance

phrases.english: But didn't we learn [in a Mishnah]:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in בכורות נב:.

phrases.english: These are the ones that do not return in the Jubilee year –
the firstborn's portion,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תְּנַן: אֵלּוּ הֵן שֶׁאֵין חוֹזְרִין בַּיּוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind אביי's claim that we already knew רבין's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That an earlier משנה already shows the husband's status, so רבין's letter was not needed for it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בכורות listing properties that do not return in the יובל year. The relevant item comes after the firstborn's portion.
